question.problem:
Let ${J}_{n}(\lambda )$ denote an $n\times n$ Jordan block with $\lambda $ on the main diagonal. Fill in the missing entries in the matrix below.
${e}^{2}$ {{field-1}} $2{e}^{2}$ {{field-2}}
${e}^{2({J}_{4}(1))}=\,\,$ $0$ ${e}^{2}$ {{field-3}} $2{e}^{2}$
$0$ $0$ ${e}^{2}$ $2{e}^{2}$
$0$ $0$ $0$ {{field-4}}
question.worked_solution:
Given a function $f$ and a Jordan block ${J}_{n}(\lambda ),$ we have

$$
f({J}_{n}(\lambda ))=[\begin{aligned}f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) & \frac{{f}^{″}(\lambda )}{2!} & ⋯ & \frac{{f}^{(n-1)}(\lambda )}{(n-1)!} \\ 0 & f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) & ⋯ & \frac{{f}^{(n-2)}(\lambda )}{(n-2)!} \\ ⋮ & ⋱ & ⋱ & ⋱ & ⋮ \\ 0 & ⋯ & 0 & f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) \\ 0 & ⋯ & ⋯ & 0 & f(\lambda )\end{aligned}].
$$

In this case, we have $f(x)={e}^{2x},$ $n=4,$ and $\lambda =1.$

Since $n=4,$ we need to compute the first $4-1=3$ derivatives of $f:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={e}^{2x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =2{e}^{2x} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =4{e}^{2x} \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =8{e}^{2x}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f({J}_{4}(1)) & =[\begin{aligned}f(1) & {f}^{′}(1) & \frac{1}{2!}{f}^{″}(1) & \frac{1}{3!}{f}^{‴}(1) \\ 0 & f(1) & {f}^{′}(1) & \frac{1}{2!}{f}^{″}(1) \\ 0 & 0 & f(1) & {f}^{′}(1) \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & f(1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2\cdot 1} & 2{e}^{2\cdot 1} & \frac{4{e}^{2\cdot 1}}{2} & \frac{8{e}^{2\cdot 1}}{6} \\ 0 & {e}^{2\cdot 1} & 2{e}^{2\cdot 1} & \frac{4{e}^{2\cdot 1}}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & {e}^{2\cdot 1} & 2{e}^{2\cdot 1} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & {e}^{2\cdot 1}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2} & 2{e}^{2} & 2{e}^{2} & \frac{4{e}^{2}}{3} \\ 0 & {e}^{2} & 2{e}^{2} & 2{e}^{2} \\ 0 & 0 & {e}^{2} & 2{e}^{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & {e}^{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
